ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, the proposed gérant, and any attorney-in-fact against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List under Regulations (EU) No 269/2014 and No 2580/2001, as amended; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the French national restrictive measures and asset-freezing orders published by the Direction generale du Tresor. PEP identification follows Code monetaire et financier Article L. 561-10 and FATF definitions in Directive (EU) 2015/849 Article 3(9); any PEP match triggers enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Screening results must be evidenced in the AML file and retained for five years after termination of the business relationship per CMF Article L. 561-33.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalites d'Entreprise (procedures.inpi.fr), operated by the Institut National de la Propriete Industrielle (INPI), with the name registered in the Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS) through the competent Greffe du Tribunal de commerce and prior availability verified via Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All mandatory corporate documents and filings must be drafted in French under Loi n° 94-665 du 16 aout 1994 (Toubon Law) and Code de commerce Article L. 123-9-2. The SARL denomination must comply with Code de commerce Article L. 223-1 and be expressed in Latin characters (French alphabet); foreign-language names and elements must be transliterated into Latin script, and foreign documents must be translated into French by a sworn translator (traducteur assermente) listed with the relevant Cour d'appel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not operate a statutory pre-incorporation name reservation for SARLs; protection accrues only upon RCS registration or prior INPI trademark filing. If the Guichet Unique refuses the proposed denomination on grounds of confusion, trademark conflict, or prohibited tokens: (1) file a written recours gracieux with the INPI directorate within two months of the electronic refusal, in accordance with the Code des relations entre le public et l'administration, Articles R. 411-1 et seq.; (2) the INPI must respond within two months, silence constituting implicit rejection; (3) challenge an explicit or implicit rejection before the competent tribunal administratif within two months of notification; (4) in the case of private trademark conflict, adopt a modified distinctive name (add a geographic element, acronym, or activity descriptor) and immediately refile through the Guichet Unique without losing the launch timeline; (5) for sensitive regulatory tokens such as 'BANQUE', a prior ministerial authorization must be obtained from the competent ministry before refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible at formation: an approved domiciliation company (agreed per Code de commerce Article L. 123-11-3) may hold the SARL registered office for an initial period not exceeding five years. However, for a SCADA/PLC integration contractor under ISIC 4321, virtual-only substance is likely to be assessed as inadequate by banking AML desks, Décennale liability insurers, URSSAF, and tax authorities; operational substance (technical office, project records, equipment storage, safety coordinator capacity) should be in place before tender submissions or credit-line underwriting.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15-20% probability per annum of unannounced physical inspection during the first three fiscal years, reflecting URSSAF, DREETS labour inspectorate, and tax audit patterns applicable to construction and electrical installation businesses under Code du travail Article L. 8211-1; likelihood increases to 25% or more where SCADA contracts involve public infrastructure or sensitive-site projects.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code) Arts. L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL constitution, capital, management and general meetings) and R. 223-1 et seq.; corporate registration under Code de commerce Arts. L. 123-1, L. 123-11 and R. 123-30 via Guichet Unique (Décret n° 2021-1475)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce; electronic single window Guichet Unique managed by INPI (formalites.entreprises.inpi.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (single digital form) with annexed Statuts constitutifs, filed electronically on the Guichet Unique portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL (capital freely fixed in the Statuts); subscribed cash contributions must be fully paid up and placed in a blocked bank account (or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations) with the attestation de dépôt de fonds issued upon funding and remitted with the filing; non-cash contributions must be fully paid at subscription; funds are released only upon delivery of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each founder subscribes to the share capital set forth in the Articles of Association and that all cash contributions are fully paid up and deposited with a French bank; that the registered office is established at [insert address] and that the company adopts its corporate governance rules under the SARL provisions of the French Commercial Code; that [Full Name], appointed Gérant, is granted the broadest powers to manage and represent the company, open bank accounts, sign operating contracts, file the incorporation dossiers through the Guichet Unique, and complete every ancillary administrative step; that any cumulative office roles are accepted; and that this resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts constitutifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding members / Notary (authentic instrument mandatory only for real estate contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the full constitutional terms: corporate name, registered office, corporate object (SCADA integration and electrical installation), share capital and division into shares, management rules, duration (99 years), and dispute arrangements. Each founder signs the articles in person or by proxy with settled powers; appoint the initial Gérant in the articles. If a notary is required, engross the statutory instrument.
required_dossiers: Signed share subscription list (acte de souscription)
Power of attorney if a signatory acts by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are challenged for formal defects, amend by a supplementary instrument (avenant) signed by all members and re-executed; restart the filing timeline from the corrected signature date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Release of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in France (or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated corporate account in the company's name before RCS filing; transfer the subscribed cash capital irrevocably and secure the blocked funds certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) evidencing that the funds are unavailable until registration is delivered. The bank releases funds only upon presentation of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Identity of the Gérant and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to incomplete KYC, supply a certified copy of the identity document and a full beneficial owner structure declaration; re-submit within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Formation Notice (Avis de constitution) in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal announcement journal (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formation announcement text to a JAL, enclosing the capital deposit certificate. The notice must identify the corporate form, name, capital amount, registered office, corporate object, duration and the Gérant's identity, strictly per Article R. 210-9 of the French Commercial Code. Retain the publisher's attestation (justificatif de publication).
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (bank certificate)
Full statutory particulars of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requests modifications, amend the notice wording and republish; adjust the filing date of the RCS request accordingly by securing a new publication attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique operated by INPI on formalites.entreprises.inpi.fr, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the single electronic declaration (Déclaration de création) with attachment of the executed Statuts, deposit certificate, legal notice attestation, identity documents, declaration of no criminal conviction for the Gérant, and capacity and professional qualification declarations under Loi n° 96-603. Each signatory validates the dossier by electronic signature. Pay the scheduled greffe and fiscal/registration fees upon submission.
required_dossiers: Certified Statuts constitutifs in final form
Attestation de dépôt de fonds (or notary certificate)
Identity document of Gérant and founders
Declaration of professional qualification/capacity for electrical works
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues an observation (query), lodge corrective documents in the Guichet Unique within 15 days; the application remains valid and the control period is reset only for the missing items.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Control, Payment of Fees and Issuance of Extrait Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (court clerk) and INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation, the Greffe registers the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, attributes the SIREN/SIRET identifier and delivers the Extrait Kbis which constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation. Verify that the Kbis recitals match the articles on corporate form SARL, capital, object, address and Gérant. Pay any statutory registration tax when invoiced.
required_dossiers: Corporate details for the Kbis recitals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where recitals are erroneous, file a corrective mention via the Guichet Unique and attach a rectification request addressed to the Greffe; the corrected Kbis is issued within three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises Compliance, Fire Inspection and Grid Operator Clearance for Substation Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DRIEETS (labor inspectorate), SDIS (fire brigade authority), and the local Inspectorate of classified installations / RTE grid operator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure the right to use the registered office (justificatif de jouissance); complete a workplace risk assessment (Document unique d'évaluation des risques); arrange fire prevention clearance for any equipment room or storage area of the site; and verify the electrical installations of the premises. For substation operations, execute the grid access convention with RTE or the distribution operator and obtain electrical operator clearance under NF C18-510.
required_dossiers: Justificatif de jouissance des locaux (lease or title)
Carte d'habilitation électrique for dispatched technicians (NF C18-510)
Grid access convention with RTE/ENEDIS if touching substation equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the labor inspectorate or SDIS notes deviations, correct the preventive measures and request a new inspection within 15 days; for RTE-controlled installations, align the technical safety file with RTE's protection plan and obtain written clearance before energization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (MTE) and DRIEETS (Directions régionales de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités); sector qualification bodies (Qualifelec and RGE) for professional capacity certifications
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat de qualification professionnelle under Article 16 of Loi n° 96-603 (electrical installation/crafts); Habilitations électriques NF C18-510; no separate operating licence is required for SCADA integration contractors

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (DREAL), Ministère de la Transition Écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from individual EIA because integration works are services rendered at third-party substations; environmental registration (Déclaration) becomes mandatory only if the contractor establishes a permanent works depot or treatment facility crossing ICPE thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Waste handling and disposal must comply with Code de l'environnement art. L. 541-1 through registered carriers; solvent-based products limited to VOC emission ceilings of Directive 2004/42/EC (max 200 g/L for industrial coatings); occupational noise exposure capped at 85 dB(A) daily (R. 4431-2 Code du travail); electrical operations to be performed under the prevention plan of the station operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by SDIS for the contractor's premises and for fire-risk zones at customer substations; structural load inspection validated under NF EN 1991-1-1 for equipment mounting bays; labor inspectorate (DRIEETS) clearance of the Document unique and collective protective measures before each work commencement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), France's national tax authority, operating through the professional portal impots.gouv.fr (Espace Abonné / Espace Professionnel); customs export clearance is separately handled by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via the DELTA-TI e-clearance platform and douane.gouv.fr; company formalities for the SARL are centralized on the INPI-operated Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the French SARL: (i) file statutory incorporation through the Guichet Unique / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE then issues SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits); (ii) the fiscal registration annex is transferred automatically to the territorial Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), which opens the corporate income tax (IS) account and issues the intra-Community VAT identification number (format FR + 11 characters); (iii) foreign entities establishing a French permanent establishment (PE) or branch file a parallel RCS/branch registration and obtain their own SIREN/SIRET and French VAT number; (iv) non-resident entities with no French PE but direct French VAT liabilities use the dedicated Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) registration procedure and, if established outside the EU, must appoint an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal). Registration is free of charge and generally completed within 1–3 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope — a SARL is by default subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) under Article 206-I CGI at the standard rate of 25% (reduced IS rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs fulfilling the ≤€10 million turnover condition); France does not accord pass-through status to SARLs by default, and the territoriality principle of Article 209-I CGI limits IS to profits derived from activities carried on in France, including French PE profits, rather than taxing the SARL's unremitted foreign-branch income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. Available elections: (1) SARL transparency election under Article 239 bis AA CGI — a qualifying SARL (capital not listed, at least 50% held directly or indirectly by individuals or by similarly qualifying SARLs, no institutional corporate majority) may opt, for a non-renewable or renewable 5-fiscal-year period, to be taxed as a société de personnes (impôt sur le revenu) instead of IS; (2) VAT option under Article 293 B CGI to waive the small-business franchise en base de TVA so the SARL can invoice French VAT and recover input VAT despite being below the mandatory registration threshold; (3) French fiscal integration election under Article 223 A CGI where a French-resident parent holding ≥95% consolidates the SARL into a single IS group; (4) hybrid mismatch rules under Article 212 bis CGI (ATAD 2 transposition) are mandatory and residual rather than elective, disallowing deductions for hybrid-instrument and hybrid-entity arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC and codified in Articles 256 to 289 CGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA: compulsory registration is triggered by annual turnover above €37,500 for service providers (SCADA/PLC integration is a services activity) and above €91,900 for sellers of goods, with reduced/tolerance thresholds of €34,400 for services and €84,900 for goods; where the applicable threshold is exceeded in a calendar year, French VAT registration becomes mandatory with effect from the day of excess; a taxable person below threshold may nonetheless elect to register; non-resident suppliers of pure B2C remote/internet services have no French registration threshold and fall within the OSS/guichet unique reporting mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not operate a pre-issuance real-time fiscal clearance or digital-stamping regime. The mandatory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform applies from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small enterprises: structured B2B e-invoices (Factur-X/UBL or PPF-native formats) must be transmitted to the buyer and to the DGFiP's Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the public API; e-reporting of transaction and payment data likewise feeds the PPF database; although invoices are not statutorily pre-authorized, the DGFiP performs near-real-time automated matching and post-issuance audit reconciliation, and export invoices must be supported by the export documentary chain where a French VAT liability is displaced by the 0%/outside-scope rule.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: 0% TVA applies under Article 262-I CGI where goods physically leave EU customs territory and the SARL (or a commissioned agent acting in its name) holds a validated customs export declaration and transport documents proving exit from the European Union. Services exports: B2B services supplied to a non-EU taxable customer — including remote SCADA programming, licences, design and off-site configuration of PLCs for foreign grids — have their place of supply outside France under Article 259-2 CGI / Article 44 of Directive 2006/112/EC and are accordingly invoiced without French VAT; services physically connected to immovable property (for example on-site commissioning of a substation located in France) are taxable at 20% under Article 259-1 CGI regardless of the foreign customer's residence, while services connected to a non-EU substation follow the situs rule and escape French VAT; intra-EU B2B services are outside French scope and are submitted to the customer's reverse charge upon VIES validation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — the SAD/DAE (Déclaration d'Échange de Biens) formally lodged on the DGDDI's DELTA-TI electronic clearance system and evidenced by the accepted Movement Reference Number (MRN) confirming exit from EU customs territory

Commercial transport documentation — bill of lading, air waybill, CMR or rail consignment note showing physical exportation to the non-EU destination, together with the commercial invoice, packing list and SCADA delivery/installation acceptance certificate

Financial remittance evidence — SWIFT MT103 or bank-account credit statement tracing receipt of the export consideration from the non-EU buyer; French law does not issue an Inward Remittance Certificate, but DGFiP requires banking corroboration on audit to confirm the commercial substance of the export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the export declaration must, however, be followed by physical exit of the goods within the 90-day window of Article 279 UCC / Article 197 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/2446, failing which the DAE is invalidated and the 0% treatment collapses. On a DGFiP contrôle fiscal, the full export chain — customs release, transport movement, commercial contract and payment trace — is scrutinized; insufficient or contradictory evidence causes the supply to be reclassified as domestic at 20% TVA, with retroactive clawback of input VAT recovered on goods, software or subcontracting costs consumed in the false export. Penalties range from 5%/10% late-filing increases, 40% for bad-faith understatement (Article 1729 CGI) and 80% for fraud or abuse of right, plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest under Article 1731-A CGI; deliberate falsification of export justifications additionally risks criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI (fine up to €500,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment) and customs penalties under the Code des Douanes, with recovery window extended up to 10 years in non-disclosure scenarios.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank, with Banque de France as the French national central bank and competent authority for relevant payment, balance-of-payments, statistical, and banking-system functions. Foreign-exchange and financial-crime oversight also involves the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution, the Autorité des Marchés Financiers, and TRACFIN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and operates within the euro area single-currency and single-payment framework. The euro is freely convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, prudential, and foreign-investment-control rules. A French SARL may generally receive foreign equity, shareholder loans, trade receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, and other legitimate cross-border payments without a general exchange-control approval. Profit remittances require distributable profits, properly approved financial statements, compliance with statutory reserve and corporate-law requirements, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner and sanctions screening, and appropriate transfer-pricing support. Payments to related parties may require arm's-length pricing, documentation, and treaty analysis. French banks may request underlying contracts, invoices, board or shareholder resolutions, tax evidence, source-of-funds evidence, and economic-purpose explanations before execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender foreign-currency export proceeds to the Banque de France, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline requiring conversion into euros. Export receipts may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted commercially at the company's discretion. The company must maintain accurate accounting and tax records, satisfy bank reporting and payment-screening requirements, comply with applicable customs and VAT rules, and respond to statistical or balance-of-payments data requests. Restricted-country, sanctioned-party, cash, and unusual-payment rules may impose separate controls. Export proceeds should be reconciled to contracts, customs documentation, invoices, shipping evidence, and customer receipts.

Capital Deposit Account / Operational Account / EUR and Foreign-Currency Accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and collections, but not a complete substitute for a French commercial-bank relationship. An EU-licensed electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards, foreign-exchange services, and limited collection functionality under its passporting, safeguarding, and product permissions. It generally cannot provide ordinary deposit-taking, a statutory capital-deposit certificate unless expressly accepted for that purpose, or the full range of French bank credit, overdraft, documentary-credit, guarantee, and project-finance services. Offshore digital EMIs outside the EU require an appropriate French or EU authorization or local regulated partner and may face enhanced correspondent-bank, sanctions, source-of-funds, data, and tax-residency scrutiny. Use of an EMI should be limited to documented operating flows after confirming safeguarding, settlement, insolvency, access to SEPA, permitted currencies, account-closure procedures, and contractual governing law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal rule that every director must appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification, remote beneficial-owner verification, certified corporate documents, and video or electronic interviews. In practice, banks may require an in-person meeting or enhanced video interview for foreign shareholders, complex ownership chains, nonresident directors, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual activities, credit facilities, cash-intensive operations, or capital-deposit accounts. The legal representative, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and controlling persons must be identified and verified. A notary may be used for certain corporate formalities, but notarization does not remove the bank's independent KYC obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent corporate identity, registration, registered-office, or beneficial-ownership information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; articles of association; certificate of incorporation or registration evidence; registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement; organization chart; UBO declaration; passports or national identity documents; residential-address evidence; management and signatory resolutions; and a written reconciliation of any name, address, director, or ownership differences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, bearer interests, or inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart through every intermediate entity; registers of shareholders and directors; constitutional documents for each holding entity; notarized or certified ownership evidence where requested; UBO attestations; tax-residency information; explanation of control rights; and evidence that the structure is commercial rather than designed to conceal ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder funding, shareholder loans, capital contributions, or incoming payments inconsistent with the stated business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; shareholder and board resolutions; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; audited or management accounts; originating-bank statements; tax returns or sale documentation where relevant; expected-flow schedule; payment-purpose narrative; and reconciliation of the remitter with the shareholder or lender.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCADA, industrial-grid, substation, automation, or dual-use technology concerns, including possible military, critical-infrastructure, or sanctioned end use.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and services catalogue; technical specifications; end-user and end-use certificates; customer, distributor, and beneficial-owner screening; destination-country analysis; export-control classification; sanctions-screening records; contract and purchase-order copies; licensing or exemption analysis; and written controls for re-export, remote access, software updates, and technical assistance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume international payments, payment-chain complexity, third-party settlement, pass-through activity, or transactions unrelated to the French SARL's stated business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling twelve-month cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier master file; expected countries and currencies; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; contract and shipping documentation; explanation of any third-party payer or payee; treasury policy; segregation-of-duties matrix; transaction-monitoring procedure; and evidence that the company is not providing unlicensed payment services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving jurisdictions, counterparties, vessels, banks, or persons subject to EU, UN, French, UK, or US sanctions or export controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty and UBO screening results; sanctions-screening methodology and timestamped records; jurisdiction-risk assessment; end-use and end-user documentation; applicable authorization or licence; payment-routing analysis; legal review of secondary-sanctions exposure where relevant; and documented escalation and rejection procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons, public-sector customers, state-owned enterprises, public procurement, or government-connected intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening evidence; senior-management approval; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds records; tender and procurement documents; beneficial-ownership and control analysis; intermediary due diligence; anti-bribery representations; commission benchmarking; conflict-of-interest checks; and enhanced transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, CRS, FATCA, VAT, permanent-establishment, or transfer-pricing inconsistencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-identification evidence; CRS self-certification; FATCA forms where applicable; VAT registration or exemption evidence; group tax-residency certificates; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; permanent-establishment analysis; and a written explanation of any non-French account, director, employee, or contracting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for overdraft, credit line, bank guarantee, performance bond, or trade-finance facility without sufficient financial history or collateral.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; signed customer contracts; backlog and order book; three-year financial projections; management accounts; group financial statements; shareholder support or guarantee; insurance policies; collateral schedule; debtor-aging report; covenant forecast; and project-level cash-flow and completion analysis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route euro capital contributions through SEPA Credit Transfer where the originating and receiving institutions participate; use SWIFT cross-border transfer where required for non-SEPA currencies or banks. Fund the SARL's capital-deposit account only from the subscribing shareholder or clearly documented contributor, using the exact legal name of the company or subscriber and a reference such as 'share capital contribution' or 'shareholder loan' consistent with the underlying agreement. For a new SARL, obtain the bank or notary capital-deposit certificate, complete incorporation, and transfer funds to the operational account after registration in accordance with the bank's release procedure. For later injections, use a documented equity increase, additional paid-in contribution, current-account advance, or loan, supported by corporate approvals and accounting entries. The bank may request subscription agreements, resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, UBO information, remitter identification, and economic-purpose documentation. There is no general French FX purpose-code regime equivalent to a mandatory Chinese-style foreign-exchange code; banks instead use payment messages, internal categories, invoice references, and regulatory reporting data. Do not split transfers to avoid controls, route funds through unrelated third parties, or describe a loan as equity or vice versa. Reconcile bank statements, general-ledger entries, shareholder accounts, and statutory filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the scheme limits and bank availability. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly represented by an MT103 legacy message or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA payments, foreign currencies, and correspondent-bank routes. Use documentary letters of credit subject to UCP 600, standby letters of credit or demand guarantees under applicable ICC rules, documentary collections under URC 522, and bank guarantees for equipment, construction, performance, advance-payment, or warranty obligations. Match each payment to the purchase order, contract, invoice, customs or shipping record where relevant, beneficiary UBO, sanctions screening, tax treatment, and Incoterms allocation. For imports of industrial automation equipment, retain technical descriptions, origin documents, export-control classification, end-use information, transport evidence, and VAT/customs records. Define maker-checker approval, dual authorization, beneficiary-change call-back controls, payment limits, sanctions screening before release, and bank-account verification independent of email instructions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an EU-regulated bank or other authorized investment firm, documented under appropriate master terms and supported by an identified underlying commercial exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable or where settlement is conventionally cash-settled, subject to counterparty authorization, applicable local-currency rules, sanctions screening, and documented exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring or long-dated funding exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation requirements where applicable, and board-approved treasury limits.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and other structured hedges only after suitability, valuation, liquidity, accounting, and maximum-loss review; avoid speculative positions unrelated to documented operating, trade, or financing exposures.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and payments, currency-denominated procurement, and centralized netting, provided the arrangement is supported by intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing documentation, and accurate exposure forecasts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return and Chiffre d'Affaires Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 2 months after financial year-end (e.g., 28 February for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 40% of tax due plus interest; non-filing may lead to administrative sanctions and potential strike-off from RCS
Penalties for late or missing audit report filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exceeds at least two of: CA > €50 million, balance sheet total > €43 million, or average employees > 500
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG) or IFRS for listed companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required; declare UBO to RCS greffe within 1 month of any change

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, with the excess taxed at 25%, if annual turnover excluding tax does not exceed EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of the capital is held by individuals or qualifying companies meeting the ownership condition.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate is the principal generally available preferential rate described above. Additional incentives may apply only if their statutory eligibility conditions are met; no sector-specific corporate tax holiday is generally available for SCADA or substation automation integration. A 3.3% social contribution on corporate tax may apply where the company’s turnover exceeds EUR 7.63 million and its IS exceeds EUR 763,000, subject to statutory allowances and exceptions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed expiry: French corporate tax losses generally carry forward indefinitely. Annual use is capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Unused losses remain available subject to continuity and change-of-activity rules. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return) with the applicable 2050–2059-SD tax package under the normal real regime; electronic transmission through the DGFiP EDI-TDFC channel, generally via an authorized provider. Form 2572-SD is used for the IS balance payment. A SARL may also have to file Form 2067-SD for specified general expenses.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; IS instalments are generally payable quarterly unless a statutory exemption applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is the second business day following 1 May, subject to the applicable DGFiP electronic-filing extension. The IS balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, ordinarily 15 May. Instalments are generally due on 15 February, 15 May, 15 August, and 15 November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the SARL’s legal name, SIREN, registered office, financial-year dates, tax office, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not change the SARL’s French resident corporate tax filing obligation. Use the SARL’s French registration and registered-office details; disclose foreign ownership where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss after reconciling accounting income to French tax rules and completing the applicable tax-package schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the French company. Do not exclude French business income merely because the shareholders or group parent are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2050–2059-SD – balance sheet, income statement, and tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the schedules applicable to the SARL’s accounting regime, including assets and liabilities, profit and loss, depreciation, provisions, tax adjustments, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French entity’s accounts and related-party balances consistently with its statutory accounts and supporting records; identify cross-border related-party transactions in the relevant disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate and pay the balance of IS after crediting instalments and applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is the French company’s obligation. A non-resident shareholder should not treat withholding on distributions as a substitute for the SARL’s IS payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose specified categories of general expenses, including qualifying hospitality, travel, and other expenses subject to reporting requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same disclosure tests to expenses involving non-resident directors, shareholders, or group entities; retain evidence of business purpose and beneficiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where the statutory conditions apply, file the annual summary of transfer-pricing policy and specified cross-border related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose reportable transactions with associated foreign entities and use amounts consistent with the accounts and transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where the statutory documentation threshold applies, file the prescribed summary of Master File and Local File information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French constituent entity must assess its own threshold and group status; a foreign parent’s documentation does not automatically discharge the French filing obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice is not remedied within the statutory period and to 80% in specified cases of fraudulent activity or concealed activity. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest, ordinarily 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Inaccurate returns may trigger additional penalties depending on the conduct and assessment circumstances.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic withholding rate on dividends paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to exemptions, applicable tax treaties, and the recipient’s status. The domestic rate may differ for specified recipients or circumstances. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-entitlement, anti-abuse, and other conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the French payer with the applicable residence certificate and prescribed treaty-relief forms, commonly Form 5000-SD and, for dividends, Form 5001-SD; other income categories use the corresponding prescribed forms. The payer should retain evidence supporting beneficial ownership, treaty residence, eligibility, and any limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements, and apply the reduced rate only when legally supportable. If withholding is made at the domestic rate, the recipient may generally seek a refund using the prescribed claim procedure and applicable time limits. Treaty rates depend on the particular France treaty and recipient facts; a tax-residence certificate alone does not establish entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding, subject to treaty reduction or an applicable EU exemption. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax, subject to statutory exceptions, including specified payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions, for which a 75% rate may apply. Treaty rates and exemptions vary by treaty, payment characterization, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The principal full-documentation threshold is generally EUR 400 million: it applies to qualifying French entities or French permanent establishments meeting the statutory turnover or gross-asset threshold, and to certain entities belonging to groups meeting that threshold. French transfer-pricing documentation requirements may also apply to entities with annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 150 million, or to entities meeting specified control or group-relationship conditions. Form 2257-SD summary reporting applies to qualifying entities under its separate statutory conditions. Thresholds and filing scope must be tested against current French law and group facts.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime for ordinary SARLs. Nevertheless, French tax law applies substance-over-form, abuse-of-law, anti-hybrid, beneficial-ownership, permanent-establishment, and anti-abuse principles. The SARL should maintain genuine governance, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational resources appropriate to its functions, decision-making evidence, and contemporaneous records supporting its contractual allocation of functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud and false corporate tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, maintaining double accounts, or intentionally submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, late-payment interest, and surcharges that may reach 80% in specified cases; criminal tax fraud may be punished by up to five years’ imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with higher penalties possible in aggravated cases under the French Tax Code and Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly participates may face personal criminal penalties, including imprisonment and fines. A court may order confiscation and other ancillary sanctions. Personal civil liability or recovery from a director is not automatic and requires a statutory basis or proof of the relevant misconduct; veil piercing is exceptional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, loans, royalties, goods, or guarantees without arm’s-length support; failing to maintain required documentation; or using unsupported profit allocation to shift French taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-profit adjustments, interest, and applicable tax penalties; failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing or incomplete documentation, subject to statutory limits and applicable assessment rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL is ordinarily liable for corporate tax and penalties. Directors may incur personal criminal or civil exposure if they knowingly organize fraud, conceal records, or satisfy statutory liability conditions; ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not by themselves pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other French-source income to a non-resident without applying, declaring, or remitting the withholding tax required by domestic law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty relief applied without sufficient eligibility evidence may be denied, with the unpaid balance recoverable from the payer under the applicable rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is generally the withholding agent. Personal liability is not automatic but may arise under applicable tax or criminal provisions where a director knowingly directs or participates in non-remittance or fraudulent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared foreign accounts, assets, or arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to make a required disclosure concerning foreign accounts or arrangements, or using undisclosed structures to conceal taxable income or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties depend on the specific disclosure duty and facts and may include fixed fines, tax reassessment, interest, and enhanced fraud surcharges. Deliberate concealment may lead to criminal tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director or representative who knowingly authorizes concealment may face personal penalties under the relevant tax or criminal provisions. Liability depends on proof and the particular statutory disclosure obligation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and proceeds of crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing, converting, or transferring proceeds of criminal activity, or using the SARL to disguise the origin or beneficial ownership of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable under French criminal law by up to five years’ imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with higher penalties for aggravated forms; confiscation and other ancillary sanctions may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other individuals who knowingly participate may be prosecuted personally and may face imprisonment, fines, and confiscation. Corporate criminal liability may also apply where the offense is committed on the company’s behalf by an organ or representative.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate asset misuse and insolvency-related misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting company funds for personal use, making unlawful distributions, concealing assets, or continuing abusive management that contributes to insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include repayment, damages, tax reassessments, insolvency proceedings, management bans, and criminal penalties where the conduct constitutes an offense such as misuse of corporate assets or bankruptcy-related misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may face civil liability, an insolvency-related contribution to the shortfall, a management ban, or criminal liability if statutory elements are established. Personal liability is fact-specific; ordinary limited liability is not automatically displaced.
